**Water Line Break with Water Shutdown and Road Closure**
A water line break has occurred in the area of Traverse Ridge Rd and Manila Dr. Draper City Water crews are on site. An emergency water shutdown is in place to facilitate the repair. See the attached map of the affected area. This map is approximate. Residents outside the highlighted area may also be affected.
Crews are evaluating the situation, so there is no estimate yet for how long the shutdown will need to be in place. Those in the affected and surrounding areas should plan to be without water for the whole day. We will provide an update as soon as we have more information.
Road Closure
Due to the water line break, the intersection at Traverse Ridge Rd and Manila Dr is at least partially closed. Draper Police are on site to help direct traffic. Please use caution and watch for detours. Avoid the area and use alternate routes if possible.
This closure will likely be in place until the repair is completed.

Today is when the Wall Fell…

The Berlin Wall collapsed under the weight of its own suppression fostered by an immoral Soviet communist system. On the evening of November 9, 1989 the people on both sides of the wall acted not knowing then if the Communist soldiers on the east side would shoot them. 

“To reject this inhuman Communist ideology is simply to be a human being. Such a rejection is more than a political act. It is a protest of our souls against those who would have us forget the concepts of good and evil.”
— Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn

This moment of “people power” had been seen previously in the 1986 bloodless toppling of a dictator in Manila. Yet the “Wall” came down just months after democracy protesters on a months long protest were crushed in June 1989 - over a thousand estimated killed in the brutal crackdown down by the Chinese Communist Party in Tiananmen Square.

The popular faith in democracy and free markets had been re-awakened by the renewed faith stoked by President Reagan. To capture the sentiments of the early Reagan presidency - three close advisors and friends of the former President joined to reflect. Their actions achieved more than any government action or initiative - it awakened the people of the world that freedom was possible and prosperous.

Watch their comments and reflections:

https://t.co/98KKRbbmo4

❗️🌊🇵🇭 - Super Typhoon Uwan Triggers Devastating Storm Surge in Gigmoto, Catanduanes

Massive waves and a powerful storm surge battered the coastal communities of Gigmoto in Catanduanes province, Philippines, as Super Typhoon Uwan intensified and approached the Bicol Region. 

The surge, driven by the typhoon's ferocious winds and low pressure, sent walls of water crashing ashore, flooding roads and nearly engulfing homes in Barangay Sicmil.

In a tragic update, authorities reported one fatality in the Bicol area directly linked to the storm surge, with residents evacuating amid ongoing heavy rains and gale-force winds. 

High-risk warnings remain in effect for several coastal barangays, urging immediate sheltering as Uwan—now the Philippines' 21st tropical cyclone of 2025—continues its path toward landfall. 

Emergency response teams are mobilizing aid, focusing on search-and-rescue operations and damage assessments in the hardest-hit zones.

🇵🇭 Aftermath of Typhoon “Kalmaegi” and Approach of a New Storm in the Philippines (November 7, 2025)

🌪 The Philippines continues to assess the damage caused by Typhoon “Kalmaegi”, which struck the central regions of the country several days ago.
According to the latest reports, the death toll has risen to 204, with 109 people still missing.

Meanwhile, another powerful typhoon — “Fung-Wong” — is approaching the archipelago.
The main impact is expected on Luzon Island, the largest and most populous island in the Philippines.
Meteorologists warn of potentially destructive winds, heavy rains, and flooding, particularly in coastal areas.

‼️🌍  Anomalous floods are happening more frequently around the globe. Almost every day, we report on several such occurrences. What is the reason? What does the statistics say? Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 8 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Tropical Cyclone UWAN
Issued at: 2:00 AM, 10 November 2025(Monday)

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Rizal, Laguna, Metro Manila, Cavite, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Pampanga, Zambales, Bataan, Quezon(General Nakar, Infanta, Real) and Batangas(Agoncillo, Alitagtag, Balayan, Balete, Bauan, Calaca, Calatagan, Tanauan, Cuenca, Laurel, Lemery, Lian, Lipa, Mabini, Malvar, Mataasnakahoy, Nasugbu, San Jose, San Luis, San Nicolas, San Pascual, Santa Teresita, Santo Tomas, Taal, Talisay, Tingloy, Tuy).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Quezon(Mauban, Atimonan, Gumaca, Plaridel, Tagkawayan, Guinayangan, Buenavista, Lopez, Calauag, Quezon, Alabat, Perez, Catanauan, General Luna, Macalelon, Pitogo, Unisan, Agdangan, Padre Burgos, Pagbilao, Tayabas, Sampaloc, Lucban, Lucena, Sariaya, Candelaria, Dolores, Tiaong, San Antonio, Jomalig, Patnanungan, Polillo, Burdeos, Panukulan) and Batangas(San Juan, Rosario, Padre Garcia, Lobo, Taysan, Ibaan, Batangas City).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Possible FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate rains affecting Quezon(San Andres, San Francisco, Mulanay, San Narciso) which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 5:00 AM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
